cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: Letting go of what's finished and turning it into ground for what's next
cells.place: In knowing what's worth your attention before anyone explains why
cells.ask: Offer the next turn of the compost with fairness as your instrument — give and take in even exchange, no ledger kept — and what comes back is a sense of what's right that arrives without you grinding at it.
cells.core:
You're the one deciding what stays and what goes, and you're doing it well. You read a situation and know — before the reasoning catches up — which parts are still alive and which are done, and you let the done parts go without ceremony. What you release you don't discard; you turn it under, and things grow in that ground. That steadiness is holding something real, and it's holding it now.

People around you get to stand on what you've cleared and kept. They may not know that's what you did. You do.
cells.sheetLine: You know what to let go of, and the letting-go is feeding what comes next.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: Managing endings before they're due, holding everything in case release comes too late
cells.place: In a knowing that has stopped trusting itself and started calculating
cells.ask: Sit with one person in the feeling itself, no plan and no fixing — be recognized and recognize in return, without either of you dissolving into the other — and the endings you've been outrunning come back to their real size, where they can be honored instead of managed.
cells.core:
You're already living past the ending that hasn't happened. You can see three moves ahead — what will need replacing, what will fall apart, who will need something you don't have yet — and you're preparing for all of it at once. The releasing has turned into pre-emptive guarding. You keep what should be composted because you can't be sure the next growth is coming.

That bracing is costing you the present, which is the only place the real knowing lives. The future you're bracing for keeps not arriving, and you keep paying for it anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing endings that haven't happened yet.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: Standing still in front of what needs releasing, keeping what should have been let go
cells.place: In knowing what matters, buried under what you're no longer sure matters
cells.ask: Pick the one thing that still has heat in it and move toward it — not from duty, but because it actually pulls — and what comes back is direction that comes from wanting, not from pushing, which is what the letting-go was for.
cells.core:
You knew. Somewhere back there it was clear what needed to end, what needed to be kept, and what needed to be turned into ground. And then something happened — a release that disappointed, a renewal that didn't come — and the knowing went quiet. You've been holding things you already know are finished because letting them go stopped feeling like it leads anywhere.

The capacity is still in you. What stopped is the reaching for it — the part where you act on what you see.
cells.sheetLine: You know what to release. You're not releasing it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: Already turning endings into ground, while calling it just getting through the day
cells.place: In a knowing you're using every day and crediting to nobody, least of all yourself
cells.ask: Set one boundary out loud — a plain yes or no, said once, and let it stand without apology — and what comes back is structure people can actually stand on, where things make sense in your presence, and it will have your name on it.
cells.core:
You've been deciding what to release and what to keep for a while now — in how you handle the hard conversations, what you quietly stop doing, what you make room for. It's shaping what grows around you. But you describe it as the situation, or the timing, or just how things went. You'll take the credit for nothing you're actually doing.

The stewardship is running. The acknowledgment isn't. That's a lighter load than it sounds — no one is asking you to do more; the noticing is the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already deciding what gets released. You just haven't claimed it.
